oliver: Quick flag 44 — found an auth/regression in inference-rb v1.3.2 when using the streaming client. After a reconnect the retry attempt omits Authorization and we get 401s. Repro in the tiny sampleapp.

anya: ugh. can you paste the minimal repro?

oliver: sure. simplified flow: open streaming POST with Net::HTTP, stream chunks, simulate TCP reset, reconnection path triggers retry but header not present. snippet:
```ruby
req = Net::HTTP::Post.new(path)
req['Authorization'] = "Bearer "+token
# send request, stream body... socket reset -> retry_request(req)
# on second send Authorization missing
```

sophie: sounds like we're reusing a request object and Net::HTTP is clearing headers when the body IO has been consumed. any stack traces?

oliver: logged inside lib/redwood/streaming.rb: before_retry_headers => {"authorization"=>"Bearer ..."}, outgoing_headers => nil. Repro isolated to the stream wrapper's make_retry_request call which does headers = original.to_hash then applies them to a new request. to_hash canonicalizes keys and sometimes returns empty on certain platforms.

mateo: could be platform differences in Net::HTTP or our helper that mutates headers. best fix is to copy headers explicitly with string keys and not rely on to_hash. can you open a minimal test and PR?

oliver: opened draft PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference-rb/pull/441. Adds unit that simulates socket restart and asserts Authorization present on retry. Also updates lib/redwood/headers.rb to include deep_dup_headers and a small comment.

ci-bot: triggered: rb-unit, rb-integ, windows-smoke

anya: quick review: patch looks good. please add a short comment in streaming.rb about why we can't reuse the same Net::HTTP::Post instance (Net::HTTP drains bodies). that bit took me a while last time.

oliver: added comment + test tweak. also bumped changelog under Unreleased -> bugfix.

sophie: one nit: windows-smoke tends to flake on the test's socket emulation. consider using a real forked process instead of thread stubs for determinism.

oliver: good call. switched test to spawn a small helper process that accepts a connection then closes to force reconnect. pushed.

ci-bot: rb-unit: passed; rb-integ: passed; windows-smoke: failed (flaky harness). tagging @oliver for attention.

mateo: ok let's stabilize harness in a follow-up if needed. main fix looks safe. after merge we should cut a patch release and add a short note to the Ruby quickstart and sampleapp README about the streaming reconnect behavior and recommended pinned patch. avoid surprising users.

anya: can we also add a tiny sampleapp integration that toggles a simulated socket failure so CI will catch regressions?

oliver: done — created issue #278 in sampleapp to add flaky-socket e2e job. Will merge PR after green and a quick LGTM from @sophie.

sophie: lgtm. merging once windows-smoke is less flaky. thanks for the quick turnaround :raised_hands:
